title: When an unasked-for gift loses value
explanation: The dictionary explains “no colour” here as a lack of value: an unsolicited thing is not valued. The line points to reception rather than a defect in the object. Something offered without being requested may be overlooked precisely because no effort was made to seek it. Our reading treats that as an observation about undervaluing what arrives easily, not proof that unsolicited help or gifts are worthless. It can sound rueful from the giver or self-mocking from someone who recognises their own neglect.
meaning_odia: ଯାଚିବା ପୂର୍ବରୁ ମିଳିଥିବା ଜିନିଷର “ରଙ୍ଗ ନାହିଁ”—ଅଭିଧାନର ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟାରେ ଏହାର ମୂଲ୍ୟ ନ ହେବାର କଥା ଅଛି। ଜିନିଷଟିର ପ୍ରକୃତ ଗୁଣ ଠାରୁ ଏଠାରେ ତାହାକୁ କେମିତି ଗ୍ରହଣ କରାଯାଉଛି, ସେଇଟି ଆଗକୁ ଆସେ। ଖୋଜିବାକୁ ବା ମାଗିବାକୁ ନ ପଡ଼ିଲେ ମିଳିଥିବା ସାହାଯ୍ୟକୁ ହାଲୁକା ଭାବେ ନେବାରେ ଏହି କଥା ଲାଗିପାରେ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ଏହା ସେହି ଅବହେଳାକୁ ଧରେ, ନ ମାଗି ମିଳିଥିବା ସବୁ ଜିନିଷ ମୂଲ୍ୟହୀନ ବୋଲି ରାୟ ଦିଏନାହିଁ।
english_summary: An unsolicited offering may receive less regard than something actively sought.
odia_summary: ନ ମାଗି ମିଳିଥିବା ସାହାଯ୍ୟ ବା ଜିନିଷର ଆଦର କମିଯାଇପାରେ।
usage_example: Original imagined example: A colleague sends useful notes before anyone asks. They remain unread until the team pays for similar guidance elsewhere. The colleague quotes the saying with a rueful smile about the notes that arrived too easily.
cultural_context: The dictionary labels the headword Sambalpur; that is a source classification, not proof of exclusive regional origin. The supplied gloss concerns value, not literal colour quality. Modern workplace use is editorial.
